mechanism_narrative: A rising GDP indicates strong economic activity, which should positively impact corporate earnings and drive up S&P 500 returns over the next 60 days.
failure_condition: If GDP growth is positive but S&P 500 returns are negative in more than 40% of the next 60-day periods, the hypothesis is falsified.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in the unemployment rate suggests economic weakness, leading to negative S&P 500 returns as investor confidence drops.
failure_condition: If UNRATE rises but S&P 500 returns remain positive in more than 50% of cases, the hypothesis fails.

mechanism_narrative: High federal funds rates indicate tight monetary policy, which can reduce borrowing and spending, leading to negative S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: If FEDFUNDS are high but S&P 500 returns are positive in over 60% of periods, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: When both unemployment and payroll employment show strength, it indicates a robust labor market, boosting consumer spending and corporate profits, leading to positive S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: If both UNRATE and PAYEMS are strong but S&P 500 returns are negative in more than 30% of cases, the hypothesis fails.

mechanism_narrative: Rising consumer prices erode profit margins and consumer purchasing power, leading to negative S&P 500 returns as inflation concerns dominate.
failure_condition: If CPI growth exceeds 5% YoY but S&P 500 returns are positive in over 50% of periods, the hypothesis is falsified.

mechanism_narrative: Increasing industrial production signals strong economic output, positively influencing S&P 500 returns as companies increase production and meet demand.
failure_condition: If INDPRO growth is positive but S&P 500 returns are negative in more than 40% of the next 60-day periods, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: Growth in both GDP and retail sales indicates strong consumer demand, leading to increased corporate revenues and positive S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: If both GDPC1 and RSAFS grow but S&P 500 returns are negative in over 35% of cases, the hypothesis fails.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in housing starts reflects strong consumer confidence and economic activity, positively impacting S&P 500 returns as related sectors benefit.
failure_condition: If HOUST increases but S&P 500 returns are negative in more than 45% of the next 20-day periods, the hypothesis is falsified.
